tasks.short: Tell regular customers about new products and prices.

steps.what: Read which new products, services and price changes apply to these regular customers.
inputs: price card when the sales office has written one
outputs: the changes to mention at this stop

steps.what: Inform each regular customer of those products, services and price changes.
inputs: the changes to mention at this stop

tasks.design: The sales office keeps one price card: product or service, old price, new price, start date, and which regular customers it applies to. The driver reads that card instead of searching the morning notes, which is the only shorter step. The driver still informs the customer at the stop. A question the card does not answer is asked of the sales office inside the lookup.
tasks.previous_blocker: Price changes sat in morning notes and in memory, so each stop started with a search for what was new.
tasks.enabler_now: Those facts already belong to the sales office. Writing them once on a card needs no new system.
tasks.still_hard: The customer still has to be told at the door. A question about a product that is not on the card, or a card nobody updated, puts the search back.
tasks.human_edge: Saying the change so this customer understands it, and noticing when the question is not on the card.
tasks.altitude: Looking up a standard price change is shorter when the card is current. The driver still informs every regular customer in person and gains no new decision.

reach.task: Keep the price card current for this route
reach.learn: To check the start date, and to ask the office before informing when the card has no line

evidence.claim: On a route the driver tells regular customers about a new product or a price change at the stop, after looking in a morning note. A single current card shortens that look. It does not remove the telling. Model knowledge.

assumptions: The boundary is one stop with one regular customer. Informing stays in person and keeps its full time.

Price card fields are product or service, old price, new price, start date, and which regular customers. The producer is the sales office, when a price or a product changes. If the card is missing or the question is not on it, the driver asks the sales office inside the lookup, before informing.
The inform step does not read a system. Reading a current card is why the lookup remains at 60: the note search drops, and questions the card cannot answer stay in that same step.
The driver does not rewrite the card. That upkeep is the sales office's 1.5 hours per 100 driver hours on this task. The driver's own upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Whether this route has a sales office that will keep the card, or the driver is the only person who hears the price changes.
How often prices or the product list change on this route.
research_questions: Of the things drivers tell regular customers, how many are standard price or product changes a card can hold, and how many are a question about this customer's own order?

incremental.description: The driver adds no recurring chore. Reading the card is the lookup step.
The sales office rewrites the price card when a product, a service or a price changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A route with no current card, or a customer who asks about a product the card does not list. The driver still searches and still informs every customer in person, so little of the lookup goes away.

tasks.short: Write the day's sales and deliveries on the record.

steps.what: See the sales and delivery quantities at the stop before they go on the daily record.
inputs: what the customer refused or was short

steps.what: Record the delivery information on the daily sales record: customer, product, quantity handed and quantity refused.
inputs: stop sheet when the planner has listed this customer and product
outputs: the day's sales and delivery line

tasks.design: The planner's stop sheet already names the customer, the product and the quantity ordered, and it leaves blank columns for quantity handed and quantity refused. The driver writes those two numbers instead of copying the names again. That is the only shorter step. Seeing what was handed over stays at the door. A stop with no line is written out in full inside the same step. The sheet stores no location and no score of the driver.
tasks.previous_blocker: The daily record was a blank page, so the driver copied the customer and the product as well as the quantities.
tasks.enabler_now: The planner already lists the stops. Two blank columns on that sheet need no new system.
tasks.still_hard: The driver still has to see what was handed over, refused or short. Goods that were not on the sheet still have to be written out.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing a refusal, a shortage or a substitute that the ordered line does not show.
tasks.altitude: Copying the customer and product names is shorter when the stop sheet has a line. The driver still counts the goods at the door and gains no new decision.

reach.task: List each stop's customer, product and quantity ordered, with two blank quantity columns
reach.learn: To write the full line when this stop is not on the sheet

evidence.claim: A route driver writes a daily sales or delivery line at the stop. A stop sheet that already names the customer and the product removes the copying of those names. The driver still counts what was handed over. Model knowledge.
Telematics and a driver app that observe location and behaviour need works-council consent.

assumptions: The boundary is one stop's sales and delivery line. Seeing the goods stays in person and keeps its full time.

Stop sheet fields are customer, product, quantity ordered, quantity handed and quantity refused. The producer of the first three is the planner, before the route. The producer of the last two is the sales driver, in this step, after seeing the goods. If the sheet has no line, the driver writes all five fields in this step, which is why it remains at 55.

No phone record is added. The sheet does not store the driver's location, hours or output. Works-council consent for a system that observes location or behaviour is not triggered, because that data is not captured.

The planner's extra upkeep is 1 hour per 100 driver hours on this task, for the two blank columns on a list the planner already makes. The driver's upkeep is zero. Writing the numbers is the record step.
unknowns: Whether the planner's list already has a line for every stop, or many deliveries are extras decided at the door.
Whether the daily record is a paper sheet in the van or a book filled in at the end of the route.
research_questions: Of the last ten routes, how many delivery lines were already on the planner's list, and how many were goods the list did not name?

incremental.description: The driver adds no recurring chore. Writing the two quantities is the record step.
The planner adds blank columns for quantity handed and quantity refused on the stop list already prepared for the route.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A stop with no planner line, or goods that were not ordered. The driver writes the full line at the door and still sees every quantity, so little of the record step goes away.

tasks.short: Hear a complaint and settle it at the stop.

steps.what: Listen to customers' complaints regarding products or services.
inputs: what is wrong with the product or the service

steps.what: Decide how to resolve those complaints for this customer.
outputs: the resolution the driver can do at this stop

steps.what: Tell the customer that resolution and carry it out when the van can.
inputs: the resolution the driver can do at this stop
outputs: what the customer was told and what was replaced

tasks.design: The driver still listens to the complaint at the stop, still decides what can be done with the goods on the van, and still tells the customer. No step is shorter. A credit the van cannot settle is taken back to the office by the driver in person. No note scores the driver, and no model drafts the reply.
tasks.previous_blocker: The complaint is whatever this customer says at the door. There is no form that contains it before the driver hears it.
tasks.enabler_now: Nothing new removes that conversation. A replacement still depends on what is on the van.
tasks.still_hard: The customer is upset, the facts are this delivery, and a promise of money the driver cannot make has to wait for the office.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing what is actually wrong, and not promising a credit the office has not allowed.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes. The driver still spends this time at the door with the customer and still decides what the van can put right.

reach.task: Settle a credit the driver could not make at the stop
reach.learn: To bring the complaint back in the customer's words and not to agree a figure at the door

evidence.claim: A route driver hears a complaint about the product or the service at the customer's door and settles what the van can replace. The listening and the answer stay with the driver. Model knowledge.

assumptions: The boundary is one complaint at one stop. Listening, the decision and the telling each stay at 100. No step is shortened.

The driver may replace goods that are on the van. The driver does not grant a credit. No complaint record is stored, so there is no structured note for a later step to read and no capture time to add.
No tool is added, so focal upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Whether this firm allows the driver to replace goods on the spot or every complaint goes back to the office.
How often a complaint is about money rather than the goods.
research_questions: Of the last ten complaints on this route, how many were settled with goods on the van, and how many needed a credit from the office?

incremental.description: No complaint tool is added, so the driver has no new upkeep on this task.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The driver still listens, still decides, and still tells the customer at the stop. No step is shortened, so no time is saved on a complaint.

tasks.short: Take payment, give change, and write the receipt.

steps.what: Collect money from customers for the goods just delivered.
inputs: the cash or the means the customer offers

steps.what: Make change and count it out to the customer.
Record transactions on customer receipts, including the amount taken and the change.

tasks.design: The driver still collects the money, still counts out the change, and still writes the receipt at the door. No step is shorter. No till is assumed, because the payment happens where there is often no screen. The receipt is written from the amounts just handled. Nothing reads a payment record the driver has not written.
tasks.previous_blocker: The amount due, the cash offered and the change are known only at the door, in the customer's presence.
tasks.enabler_now: Nothing new removes the counting or the handing over. A printed receipt would still need the same amounts entered at the stop.
tasks.still_hard: The cash has to be counted in front of the customer, and a wrong change is the driver's to put right.
tasks.human_edge: Counting the notes and the change before they leave the driver's hand.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes. The driver still takes the payment, still makes the change, and still writes the receipt.

reach.task: Hand over cash and wait for change and a receipt
reach.learn: Not to treat an unticked receipt as proof the change was given

evidence.claim: A route driver collects cash at the door, counts out the change, and writes a receipt by hand. That counting and that writing stay at the stop. Model knowledge.

assumptions: The boundary is one payment at one stop. Collecting the money, making the change and writing the receipt each stay at 100. No step is shortened.

No till, card record or priced line is produced for a machine. The amount due is what the driver and the customer just agreed. The receipt fields, written by the driver in the last step, are the goods, the amount taken and the change. There is no earlier structured payment for this step to copy.
No tool is added, so focal upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Whether this route is paid in cash, or some customers pay on account and the driver only writes a delivery note.
Whether a handheld till is already in the van.
research_questions: Of the last ten stops, how many were cash with change, and how many were an account with no money at the door?

incremental.description: No payment tool is added, so the driver has no new upkeep on this task.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The driver still collects the money, still counts the change, and still writes the receipt at the door. No step is shortened, so no time is saved on a payment.

role.altitude: The sales driver still informs every regular customer, still counts the goods at the door, still hears complaints, and still takes the money and the change. A price card from the sales office shortens only the search for a standard price change. A stop sheet from the planner shortens only the copying of customer and product names. No diagram of the route is drawn by a machine, and no record stores the driver's location or a score.
reach: Sales office: a price card with no line for this question. Learn the current price before telling the customer.
Planner: a stop with no line on the sheet. Learn to write the full delivery line at the door.
Customer: a complaint the van cannot settle. Learn that the driver does not agree a credit at the door.
skills_to_grow: Tell only the products, services and price changes the card lists, and ask the office when the customer asks about something else.
Write the full delivery line when the stop sheet has no row for these goods.
Do not promise a credit at the door, and do not record the driver's location or output.
role.ambitious_version: The sales office keeps one price card, and the planner leaves two blank quantity columns on the stop sheet. The driver still informs every customer, still counts the goods, still listens to complaints, and still takes the money.
